subject: Archaeology
title: The Mary Rose: Henry VIII's Flagship
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Mary Rose: Henry VIII's Flagship.

hook.text: Henry VIII watched helplessly from shore as his favorite warship sank during a French attack in 1545.

buildup.text: The Mary Rose capsized in the Solent, drowning most of its 400-man crew. Open gun ports let water flood in as it turned.

discovery.text: Raised in 1982, the wreck contained 19,000 artifacts: longbows, medical kits, backgammon sets.

twist.text: DNA analysis of the crew revealed men from Africa and Southern Europe — Tudor England was more diverse than assumed.

climax.text: The Mary Rose is now displayed in Portsmouth with its artifacts — a complete snapshot of Tudor life at sea.

punchline.text: A king's warship sank with a pet dog, board games, and a multinational crew.

quiz.question: What did DNA analysis of the Mary Rose crew reveal?
options: All crew members were from the same English county
The crew included men from Africa and Southern Europe — Tudor England was diverse
Most sailors were former prisoners pressed into naval service

details.summary: The Mary Rose, Henry VIII's warship that sank in 1545, was raised from the Solent in 1982 in one of history's most ambitious marine salvage operations. The preserved hull and 19,000 artifacts provide an unparalleled view of Tudor naval warfare, daily life, and the 500 crew members who perished.
details.whyItMatters: The Mary Rose is a time capsule of Tudor England preserved in mud. Personal possessions, weapons, medical supplies, and even a pet dog create an intimate portrait of 16th-century life impossible to construct from documents alone.
takeaways: The Mary Rose sank in 1545 and was raised in 1982
19,000 artifacts reveal Tudor naval life in extraordinary detail
The raising was one of the most ambitious salvage operations ever

faq.question: Why did the Mary Rose sink?
faq.answer: During a battle with the French fleet, the ship heeled sharply while turning and water flooded through open gun ports close to the waterline. The crew could not close the ports in time. Anti-boarding netting may have trapped sailors, contributing to the loss of nearly all 500 crew.

faq.question: What was found on board?
faq.answer: Longbows (the largest collection ever found), iron and bronze cannon, navigation instruments, a barber-surgeon's medical chest with tools and medicines, personal items like rosaries and gaming sets, and skeletal remains of crew analyzed for diet, disease, and geographic origin.
